info.name: VectorText
info.comment: Extends the Vector class with support for generating text.

description.p: To create text along a path, set the Vector.GuidePath field with a reference to any Vector object that generates a path. The following extract illustrates the SVG equivalent of this feature:
description.pre:
<defs> <path id="myTextPath2" d="M75,20 l100,0 l100,30 q0,100 150,100"/> </defs>
<text x="10" y="100" stroke="#000000"> <textPath xlink:href="#myTextPath2"/> </text>
description.p: Support for bitmap fonts is included. This feature is implemented by drawing bitmap characters to an internal VectorImage and then rendering that to the viewport as a rectangular path. It is recommended that this feature is only used for fast 1:1 rendering without transforms. The user is otherwise better served through the use of scalable fonts.

action.name: Clipboard
action.comment: Copies, cuts or pastes selected text through the system clipboard.

input.param: The mode that will be used to shift data between the target object and clipboard system.

description.p: CLIPMODE::COPY copies SelectedText as UTF-8. CLIPMODE::CUT copies the selection and removes it only after the clipboard accepts the text. Both operations leave the clipboard and text unchanged when nothing is selected or VTXF::SECRET is set in TextFlags.

CLIPMODE::PASTE replaces the selection, or inserts at the cursor when nothing is selected. CRLF and CR line endings are normalised to LF. With LineLimit set to 1, each line ending becomes a space. Other line limits reject a paste that would exceed the limit after replacing the selected rows. CharLimit truncates each resulting line in character columns, matching keyboard editing. Text after a null byte is ignored.
Cut and paste require VTXF::EDITABLE. Copy does not change the selection or call OnChange. Cut and paste call OnChange once if the text changes.

result.error: The operation completed, or there was nothing to copy or change.
The clipboard mode is not supported.
No text is available to paste.
The clipboard file is too large to read.
The Clipboard object could not be created.
The clipboard file could not be opened.
Cut or paste was requested for non-editable text.

input.param: The line number that you want to delete. If negative, the last line will be deleted.

description.p: This method deletes lines from a text object. You only need to specify the line number to have it deleted. If the line number does not exist, then the call will fail. The text graphic will be updated as a result of calling this method.

result.error: The Line value was out of the valid range.

method.name: SelectArea
method.prototype: ERR vt::SelectArea(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Row, INT Column, INT EndRow, INT EndColumn)

input.param: The line at which the selection starts.
The character column at which the selection starts.
The line at which the selection ends. If negative, the last line is used.
The character column at which the selection ends. If negative, the end of the line is used.

description.p: SelectArea() marks a region of text as selected, starting at the position given by Row and Column. The cursor is moved to the end of the region at EndRow and EndColumn, which may come before the start for a reversed selection. Columns are character positions, so UTF-8 sequences count as one column each. A negative EndRow refers to the last line and a negative EndColumn refers to the end of its line, so SelectArea(0, 0, -1, -1) selects all of the text. Positions beyond the text are clamped to its limits.

While an area is selected the AREA_SELECTED bit is set in TextFlags. The next character typed, or a press of Backspace, Delete, Clear or Enter, will replace or delete the selected text. Moving the cursor deselects the area.
Editable text displays the selected area with the SelectFill painter. The highlight is hidden when focus is lost and restored when focus returns; the selection range is retained.
If the start and end positions are identical, the cursor is moved and no area is selected.

field.name: Align
field.comment: Defines the alignment of the text string.

description.p: This field specifies the horizontal alignment of the text string. The standard alignment flags are supported in the form of ALIGN::LEFT, ALIGN::HORIZONTAL and ALIGN::RIGHT.
In addition, the SVG equivalent values of start, middle and end are supported and map directly to the formerly mentioned align flags.

field.name: CharLimit
field.comment: Limits the total characters allowed in the string.

description.p: Set the CharLimit field to limit the number of characters that can appear in the string. The minimum possible value is 0 for no characters. If the object is in edit mode then the user will be unable to extend the string beyond the limit.
Note that it is valid for the String length to exceed the limit if set manually. Only the display of the string characters will be affected by the CharLimit value.

field.name: CursorColumn
field.comment: The current column position of the cursor.

field.name: CursorRow
field.comment: The current line position of the cursor.

field.name: DX
field.comment: Adjusts horizontal spacing on a per-character basis.

description.p: If a single value is provided, it represents the new relative X coordinate for the current text position for rendering the glyphs corresponding to the first character within this element or any of its descendants. The current text position is shifted along the x-axis of the current user coordinate system by the provided value before the first character's glyphs are rendered.

If a series of values is provided, then the values represent incremental shifts along the x-axis for the current text position before rendering the glyphs corresponding to the first n characters within this element or any of its descendants. Thus, before the glyphs are rendered corresponding to each character, the current text position resulting from drawing the glyphs for the previous character within the current ‘text’ element is shifted along the X axis of the current user coordinate system by length.

If more characters exist than values, then for each of these extra characters: (a) if an ancestor Text object specifies a relative X coordinate for the given character via a DX field, then the current text position is shifted along the x-axis of the current user coordinate system by that amount (nearest ancestor has precedence), else (b) no extra shift along the x-axis occurs.

field.name: DY
field.comment: Adjusts vertical spacing on a per-character basis.

description.p: This field follows the same rules described in DX.

field.name: Descent
field.comment: The font descent measured in pixels.

description.p: Use Descent to retrieve the height of the font descent region, which is the space reserved below the baseline. The value is measured in the same pixel units as FontSize, so it is unaffected by the display density and is subject to the same transforms as the text.

field.name: DisplayHeight
field.comment: The font height measured in pixels.

description.p: Use DisplayHeight to retrieve the height of the font, measured in the same pixel units as FontSize. For scalable fonts the value is the sum of the ascent and Descent. The value does not account for the display density or for transforms applied to the text.

field.name: DisplaySize
field.comment: The FontSize converted to points.

description.p: DisplaySize returns the FontSize converted from pixels to points at the fixed reference density of 96 DPI, calculated as FontSize * 72 / 96 and truncated to an integer. For example, a FontSize of 16 returns 12. The display density is not taken into account.
This value matches Point, except that Point is rounded to the nearest integer rather than truncated.

field.name: Face
field.comment: Defines the font face/family to use in rendering the text string.

description.p: The family name of the principal font for rendering text is specified here.

It is possible to list multiple fonts in CSV format in case the first-choice font is unavailable. For instance, Arial,Noto Sans would select the Noto Sans font if Arial was unavailable in the font database. The name of the closest matching font will be stored as the Face value.

field.name: Fill
field.comment: Defines the fill painter using SVG's IRI format.

description.p: The painter used for filling a vector path can be defined through this field using SVG compatible formatting. The string is parsed through the ReadPainter function. Please refer to it for further details on valid formatting.
Fallback colours and layered fill painters are supported in the same way as the Vector.Fill field. Please refer to it for further details.

field.name: Focus
field.comment: Refers to the object that will be monitored for user focussing.

description.p: A VectorText object in edit mode will become active when its nearest viewport receives the focus. Setting the Focus field to a different vector in the scene graph will redirect monitoring to it.
Changing this value post-initialisation has no effect.

field.name: Font
field.comment: Copies key meta information from a Font or other VectorText to create a matching text object.

description.p: To create a VectorText object that uses a matching typeset from another Font or VectorText object, set this field with a reference to that object. This can only be done prior to initialisation and the other object must have been initialised.

field.name: FontSize
field.comment: Defines the vertical size of the font.

description.p: The FontSize is equivalent to the SVG font-size attribute and refers to the height of the font from the dominant baseline to the hanging baseline. This would mean that a capitalised letter without accents should fill the entire vertical space defined by FontSize.

The default unit of FontSize is the pixel, and the value defines the em size of the font. A FontSize of 16 produces an em that is 16 pixels high in the text's coordinate space, which matches the behaviour of CSS and SVG. The display density is not applied, so the size on the display only changes if the text is transformed.

Standard unit measurements such as px, pt, pc, in, cm, mm and em are supported by appending them after the numeric value. Physical units are converted to pixels at a fixed reference density of 96 DPI, irrespective of the display, so 12pt is equivalent to 16px. Clients that need a physical size on a high density display must scale the value themselves, for example by multiplying a point size by DisplayDPI / 96. The em unit is fixed at 16 pixels. The final value is rounded to the nearest whole pixel, so 11pt (14.67px) becomes 15px. A size that rounds to less than one pixel is rejected with ERR::OutOfRange.
Reading FontSize returns the pixel size as a numeric string without a unit suffix.

NOTE: The FontSize is derived from information defined by the font author. Due to opinionated views on how font height is determined, the value is not transferrable between fonts. The primary difference is that some fonts will include the space for accents in the FontSize value, while others will not.

field.name: FontStyle
field.comment: Determines font styling.

description.p: Unique styles for a font can be selected through the FontStyle field. Conventional font styles are Bold, Bold Italic, Italic and Regular (the default). Because TrueType fonts can use any style name that the designer chooses such as Thin, Narrow or Wide, read fonts:fonts.cfg for a definitive list of available style names.
Errors are not returned if the style name is invalid or unavailable.

field.name: InlineSize
field.comment: Enables word-wrapping at a fixed area size.

description.p: The inline-size property allows one to set the wrapping area to a rectangular shape. The computed value of the property sets the width of the rectangle for horizontal text and the height of the rectangle for vertical text. The other dimension (height for horizontal text, width for vertical text) is of infinite length. A value of zero (the default) disables the creation of a wrapping area.

field.name: LineLimit
field.comment: Restricts the total number of lines allowed in a text object.

description.p: Set the LineLimit field to restrict the maximum number of lines permitted in a text object. It is common to set this field to a value of 1 for input boxes that have a limited amount of space available.

field.name: LineSpacing
field.comment: The number of pixels from one line to the next.

description.p: This field can be queried for the vertical advance between each line of text. The value is measured in the same pixel units as FontSize, so it is unaffected by the display density and is subject to the same transforms as the text.

field.name: OnChange
field.comment: Receive notifications for changes to the text string.

description.p: Set this field with a function reference to receive notifications whenever the text string changes.
The callback function prototype is void Function(*VectorText).

field.name: Point
field.comment: Returns the point-size of the font.

description.p: Reading the Point value will return the point-size of the font, calculated as FontSize * 72 / 96 and rounded to the nearest integer. The conversion uses the fixed reference density of 96 DPI that applies to all FontSize units, not the density of the display.

field.name: Rotate
field.comment: Applies vertical spacing on a per-character basis.

description.p: Applies supplemental rotation about the current text position for all of the glyphs in the text string.

If multiple values are provided, then the first number represents the supplemental rotation for the glyphs corresponding to the first character within this element or any of its descendants, the second number represents the supplemental rotation for the glyphs that correspond to the second character, and so on.
If more numbers are provided than there are characters, then the extra numbers will be ignored.
If more characters are provided than numbers, then for each of these extra characters the rotation value specified by the last number must be used.

If the attribute is not specified and if an ancestor 'text' or 'tspan' element specifies a supplemental rotation for a given character via a 'rotate' attribute, then the given supplemental rotation is applied to the given character (nearest ancestor has precedence). If there are more characters than numbers specified in the ancestor's 'rotate' attribute, then for each of these extra characters the rotation value specified by the last number must be used.

This supplemental rotation has no impact on the rules by which current text position is modified as glyphs get rendered and is supplemental to any rotation due to text on a path and to 'glyph-orientation-horizontal' or 'glyph-orientation-vertical'.

field.name: SelectColumn
field.comment: Indicates the column position of a selection's beginning.

description.p: If the user has selected an area of text, the starting column of that area will be indicated by this field. If an area has not been selected, the value of the SelectColumn field is undefined.
To check whether or not an area has been selected, test the AREA_SELECTED bit in the TextFlags field.

field.name: SelectFill
field.comment: The painter used to highlight selected editable text.

description.p: Accepts the same colours, paint servers and layered painters as Vector.Fill. The default is rgba(0,120,215,0.35). The highlight is drawn over the glyphs, so a translucent painter keeps them legible. Selection highlights follow the text's transforms and are hidden while focus is lost.

field.name: SelectRow
field.comment: Indicates the line position of a selection's beginning.

description.p: If the user has selected an area of text, the starting row of that area will be indicated by this field. If an area has not been selected, the value of the SelectRow field is undefined.
To check whether or not an area has been selected, test the AREA_SELECTED bit in the TextFlags field.

field.name: SelectedText
field.comment: The selected text, with line breaks separating selected lines.

description.p: Returns an empty string when there is no selection or the SECRET flag is set in TextFlags.

field.name: ShapeInside
field.comment: Reference a vector shape to define a content area that enables word-wrapping.

description.p: This property enables word-wrapping in which the text will conform to the path of a Vector shape. Internally this is achieved by rendering the vector path as a mask and then fitting the text within the mask without crossing its boundaries.
This feature is computationally expensive and the use of InlineSize is preferred if the text can be wrapped to a rectangular area.

field.name: ShapeSubtract
field.comment: Excludes a portion of the content area from the wrapping area.

description.p: This property can be used in conjunction with ShapeInside to further restrict the content area that is available for word-wrapping. It has no effect if ShapeInside is undefined.

field.name: String
field.comment: The string to use for drawing the glyphs is defined here.

description.p: The string for drawing the glyphs is defined here in UTF-8 format. Lines are separated by line feeds.

The retrieved string contains every line of the text, separated by line feeds, including any changes made by the user while editing. Line breaks introduced by word-wrapping (see InlineSize) are not included.

field.name: TextFlags
field.comment: Optional flags.

field.name: TextLength
field.comment: The expected length of the text after all computations have been taken into account.

description.p: The purpose of this attribute is to allow exact alignment of the text graphic in the computed result. If the computed text width does not match this value, then the text will be scaled to match the TextLength.

field.name: TextWidth
field.comment: The pixel width of the widest line in the String field.

description.p: This field will return the pixel width of the widest line in the String field. The result is not modified by transforms.

field.name: TotalLines
field.comment: The total number of lines stored in the object.

field.name: Weight
field.comment: Defines the level of boldness in the text.

description.p: The weight value determines the level of boldness in the text. A default value of 400 will render the text in its normal state. Lower values between 100 to 300 render the text in a light format, while high values in the range of 400 - 900 result in boldness.
Please note that setting the Weight will give it priority over the FontStyle value.

field.name: X
field.comment: The x coordinate of the text.

description.p: The x-axis coordinate of the text is specified here as a fixed value. Scaled coordinates are not supported.

field.name: Y
field.comment: The base-line y coordinate of the text.

description.p: The Y-axis coordinate of the text is specified here as a fixed value. Scaled coordinates are not supported.
Unlike other vector shapes, the Y coordinate positions the text from its base line rather than the top of the shape.

constants.comment: Universal values for alignment of graphics and text

constants.const: Automatically set if a region of text has been selected.
Enable animated blinking (not supported - exists as SVG dummy option).
Allow user editing of the text if the nearest viewport has the focus.
Allow user editing of the text if the nearest viewport has the focus.
Enable a strike-through line in the text.
Disables support for system-keys that enable common key combinations such as Ctrl-C, Ctrl-X etc.
Turns on overwrite mode (if off, insert mode is enabled).
Rasterise glyphs to a texture cache for very fast rendering. This feature is not compatible with scalable graphics conventions.
